subject: satisfactory choice for L given target precision, line transects

messages.subject: satisfactory choice for L given target precision, line transects
parts:
Dear list,=0A=0AI am trying to refine a 2nd year of a study with results f=
rom the first year. Following steps in DS text 2001, pp 242- 244,=A0I went=
to estimate total line length L to be surveyed given target CV(D) of 10%.=
=0AFor planning purposes, a recommended value for b =3D 3. But if results =
from an operational year are in hand, these can be used to estimate b in o=
rder to plug that in and come up with a refined estimate of L.=A0=0A=0ATot=
al line length (Lo) from my first year of line transect surveys was 6118 k=
m. The sample size (no) was 820. Est'd CV(D) was roughly .13 or 13%.=0A=0A=
When I went to calculate b from the data, as b ~ no=A0=A0x {cv(D)}2, I cam=
e up with a value for b of about 13 =A0--> =A0820 x .016 =3D 13.=A0=0AUsin=
g this est'd b and target cv(D) of 10%, total line length L works out to b=
e between 9,600 - 10,400 km.=A0=0AFirst I found L by plugging b ~13 into e=
qn 7.1 and got L =3D 9,620. =A0Then I did it a different way using eqn 7.5=
and got L =3D 10,339.=0A=0A=0AFinally my question: assuming I've done it =
correctly and est'd b and L values about right, can anyone comment as whet=
her the size of b of 13 is cause for major concern. =A0=0AMy detection fun=
ction does have a relatively narrow shoulder, so I expected b to be > 3.=A0=
In addition, the study involves surveys of clustered population in which g=
roup size varies tremendously -- flocks can be as small as a handful of in=
dividuals to thousands, so this might be the main culprit.. and in that ca=
se, a satisfactory choice for L could be much higher still.=A0=0A=0APlease=
can anyone comment on whether this is indicative of an extreme situation =
requiring modification to survey plan?=0A=0AThanks in advance=0A=0A-------=
